sections.text:
On a beautiful sunny morning, a black-feathered crow was flying in search of food in the forest.

Suddenly, the crow spotted a large, yellow, delicious piece of cheese lying on the window of one of the country cottages.

The crow swooped down very quickly and snatched the piece of cheese with its strong beak, then flew high and landed on the branch of a huge, tall oak tree to enjoy its delicious meal in peace.

Meanwhile, there was a cunning and hungry fox wandering under the trees looking for prey or something to eat.

The fox smelled the delicious smell of cheese, so he raised his head and saw the crow standing on the branch with cheese in his mouth.

The cunning fox thought of a clever trick to fool the crow and make him drop the piece of cheese without making any effort to climb the tree.

The fox stood under the tree, looked at the crow with a wide smile, and said in a loud, hypocritical voice: “Good morning, Mr. Crow! What a beautiful day worthy of your beauty!”

The crow looked down in surprise, but did not open his mouth for fear that the cheese would fall.

The fox continued his false praise, saying: “Oh my God! I have never seen a bird with your beauty and the splendor of your shiny black feathers in my life. They shine in the sun like luxurious black silk!”

The crow felt very arrogant. He was accustomed to people making fun of his black color and his annoying voice, and no one had ever praised him before.

The fox completed his malicious plan and said: “I am absolutely sure that a bird has this extraordinary beauty. It must have a sweet and beautiful voice that surpasses the sound of nightingales and nightingales!”

Then he added, pleadingly: “Please, my lord, the crow, make me hear just one song with your enchanting voice, so that I may crown you king of all the birds of the forest!”

The crow's mind was filled with vanity and pride, and he wanted to prove to the fox that he had a wonderful voice.

The crow took a deep breath, opened its beak wide to sing, and shouted in its usual annoying voice: “QAQ! QAQ! QAQ!”

As soon as he opened his beak, the large golden piece of cheese fell directly into the mouth of the cunning fox, which was eagerly waiting for it under the tree.

The fox swallowed the piece of cheese in one bite, then wiped his mouth with his tongue and said, laughing: “Thank you for this delicious meal, my naive friend!”

Then the fox added as he left: “Your voice is loud but annoying, and your mind is completely empty! Let this be a lesson to you; never trust someone who exaggerates false praise and flattery towards you.”

The sad and hungry crow remained on the branch, deeply regretting his arrogance and believing the fox’s sweet words, and he learned a harsh lesson that he would not forget for the rest of his life.
